Colorful plumage often functions as a signal—for example, to attract a mate. Alternatively, drab colors can be used for camouflage. However, color can have functions beyond signaling and camouflage. This is because pigments, the molecules embedded in feather tissues to produce a broad range of colors, can also influence other aspects of feathers, ranging from mechanical strength to thermoregulatory properties.

Ancient climate records reveal how East Asian monsoon shifted abruptly into cold and drought
items.summary: How does climate change affect the East Asian monsoon? Researchers from Utrecht University's Faculty of Geosciences, together with colleagues at research institutes in China and Belgium, are investigating this question by looking back 250,000 years. They found that, over long timescales, the monsoon system tracks changes in incoming solar radiation caused by variations in Earth's orbit and tilt. But when radiation falls below a certain threshold, abrupt periods of extreme cold and drought occur, particularly when atmospheric CO₂ concentrations are low. The study was published in Communications Earth & Environment.

items.summary: High yield 5.441% vs 5.437% WI Tail of 0.4 basis points Bid-to-cover 2.36x vs 2.44x average Dealers awarded 11.39% vs 9.49% average The US Treasury sold $25 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday in a disappointing auction that adds to signs of softening demand at the long end of the curve. The auction stopped at 5.441%, a 0.4 basis point tail compared to the 5.437% when-issued yield. That's a deterioration from last month's 0.1 basis point tail and compares unfavourably with the six-auction average of a 0.1 basis point stop-through. The bid-to-cover ratio fell to 2.36x from 2.54x previously, also below the 2.44x six-auction average. The breakdown of buyers wasn't particularly encouraging either. That would leave the Fed facing a more difficult balancing act: raising rates enough to contain inflation without unnecessarily damaging the economy. It’s hard to overstate the importance of the turnovers that the UCLA Bruins have forced this season. The team leads the nation with 27 turnovers. Typically, turnovers forced can be a bit streaky, as it often requires a bit of good fortune to force takeaways but the UCLA defense is putting that belief to the test. Defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler has transformed the Bruin defense into a ball-seeking machine and the group hasn't shown many signs of slowing down. UCLA is averaging three turnovers per game this season but forced only one turnover against Illinois last week when Bruin defensive back Scooter Jackson picked off Drake Lindsey.

For the first time since 1971, the Longhorns will wear their home jerseys on the road. UT will wear Burnt Orange at LSU, who traditionally wear white. Texas last wore its home uniform on the road against UCLA at the Los Angeles Colosseum. UCLA also wore its regular powder blue home jersey in the 28-10 Longhorns victory. Wearing your colored jerseys on the road was more common back then. But in the early 1980s, the NCAA changed the rules. In 1982, the NCAA had altered the "jersey rule," requiring teams to wear the school color jerseys for home games. LSU, who traditionally wore white at home, wore purple jerseys for all home games from 1983 to 1994.

Popular tourist beaches at Margate and Ramsgate are among the areas affected by the spill. Thanet District Council (TDC) reported the incident on Wednesday evening. The source of the oil has not been identified. The local authority said the decision to close access to beaches "had not been taken lightly". A spokesperson for TDC urged people, particularly dog walkers, to avoid the affected areas, and to report any deposits of oil on beaches to them.

When the Detroit Lions take on the New England Patriots in Germany this weekend, it will be a head-to-head matchup of former players for their respective teams. Let's take a little walk down memory lane, back to Dec. 3, 2006, when the 2-9 Lions traveled to face the 9-2 Patriots looking to play spoilers down the stretch. Today in Boston Celtics history, Frederick Robert Robey extended his contract with the team. Robey became part of Boston's roster in January 1979, dealt to Boston by the Indiana Pacers for forward Billy Knight, and up to that moment of his career in the NBA, he had been something of an iron man, having missed a mere two contests in total suiting up for the Celtics. The Democratic candidate won in a southern state that had not seated a black senator since 1874. After winning a close race in Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom will become the state's first black US senator for more than 150 years, and the third in history. It is a historic result in the deeply conservative southern state that last sent a Democrat to the US Senate in 1982, and had not seated a black senator since 1875. Colom follows Hiram Revels, who became the first black person ever to serve in the chamber when he was seated from 1870 to 1871, and Blanche Bruce, whose term ran from 1875 to 1881. Revels and Bruce were both members of the Republican Party.
